papers.title: Tropicalization and Polyhedral Completions of Weyl Algebras
papers.abstract: We construct weighted and polyhedral completions of the Weyl algebra over a complete nonarchimedean field and organize them into a structure sheaf on a polyhedral $G$-site. For discretely valued fields, we prove two-sided flatness for $\Gamma$-rational polyhedral completions, yielding exact base change for finitely generated $D$-modules. For compact integral polyhedra, we also construct finite-type integral models whose special fibers are toric face rings and describe the reduction of Gauss points in terms of toric strata.

papers.title: Extended Tropical Characteristic Fibers and Slopes of Binomial D-Modules
papers.abstract: For a holonomic $D$-module, we consider the extended tropicalization of the reduced $L$-characteristic fiber along the family $L_s=F+(s-1)V_Y$. For $A$-hypergeometric systems, this tropical fiber determines the complete $(A,L)$-umbrella and hence recovers the classical slopes. We extend this result to holonomic binomial $D$-modules, for which the tropical jump parameters are exactly the classical slopes at the origin. As an application, a holonomic binomial $D$-module is regular holonomic if and only if there are no tropical jumps along any coordinate subspace.

papers.title: Weighted flip graphs from cyclic quantum mutations: pentagon inequalities and exponential separations
papers.abstract: Positive cyclic quantum mutations at a third root of unity induce an explicit weight on polygon flip graphs. We study the resulting discrepancy between minimum flip count and minimum accumulated normalization loss. Every pentagon three-to-two replacement strictly decreases weight, and in connected types $A_1$, $A_2$, and $A_3$ every minimum-weight path is a flip geodesic. In type $A_4$, however, a six-flip path has smaller weight than the unique five-flip geodesic. A compatible positive projective gluing construction amplifies this example to an exponential success-probability separation in every connected type $A_n$, $n\ge4$. We also give a quantitative perturbation bound preserving the separation. The low-rank minimality statement has an exhaustive finite certificate; the pentagon inequality and the all-rank construction are analytic. In the associated sequential postselection model, differences of path weights determine success-probability ratios independently of the input state. The comparison holds for separately normalized exact mutation steps.

papers.title: A reciprocal Schoenberg inequality and its extensions
papers.abstract: We study reciprocal moments of the critical points of a polynomial with a simple zero at the origin. A positive similarity transforms a reciprocal derivative companion into a complex symmetric matrix. This gives a short proof of the reciprocal Schoenberg inequality and a refinement for every elementary symmetric function. We determine the optimal constants in the corresponding inequalities for every positive exponent, including the sublinear range, and extend the results to arbitrary positive charges. We also characterize the normal powers of the companion and of its symmetric representative. The resulting criterion gives the complete equality cases in two quartic inequalities and explains the appearance of noncollinear equality configurations at higher orders. We also obtain a closed generating determinant and a quantitative collinearity estimate.

papers.title: Linear Rank Nonincreasing and Preserving Maps between Matrix Spaces
papers.abstract: We classify linear maps $\phi$ between possibly different rectangular matrix spaces over a field $\mathbb F$ with $|\mathbb F|\ge5$ such that $\operatorname{rank} \phi(A)\le2$ whenever $\operatorname{rank} A\le2$. Every such map has one of six forms. If its image contains a matrix of rank greater than two, then $\phi(A)=MAN$ or $\phi(A)=MA^{\top}N$ for fixed matrices $M,N$. The remaining forms have images consisting entirely of matrices of rank at most two, including an exceptional form arising from $3\times3$ alternating matrices. As a consequence, we characterize linear maps preserving rank exactly two. We also prove that rank-$k$ preservation implies rank-$k$ nonincrease when $|\mathbb F|>k+2$, and that rank-$k$ nonincrease implies rank-$\ell$ nonincrease for every admissible $\ell\ge k$ when $|\mathbb F|>k+1$. The classification uses the fact that the Chow rank of the generic $3\times3$ determinant is five, connecting the rank preserver problem with product decompositions of polynomials.

papers.title: Algebraic Vector Fields of Connected Semi-simple Matrix Groups are 3-generated
papers.abstract: We show that the Lie algebra of algebraic vector fields for any connected, semi-simple matrix group over $\mathbb{F}$, for $\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}$, can be generated by three $\mathbb{F}$-complete algebraic vector fields.

papers.title: Composition factor algebras and finite representation type
papers.abstract: An Artin algebra is called a composition factor algebra if its indecomposable finitely generated modules are determined, up to isomorphism, by their composition factors. We prove that every composition factor algebra is representation-finite. This settles a conjecture of Auslander, Reiten and Smal\o. We also give criteria for comma categories and factorization categories to be of finite representation type.

papers.title: Descent and Decomposability of Algebras of Exponent 2 in characteristic 2
papers.abstract: We define an invariant of central simple algebras of degree 8 and exponent 2 over fields of characteristic 2. It is built from the discriminant Pfister forms of symplectic involutions, takes values in a quotient of the third part of the graded group associated to the fundamental filtration of the Witt group of quadratic forms, and vanishes on tensor products of three quaternion algebras, thus giving a necessary condition for decomposability. Variants of the consctuction yield necessary and sufficient conditions for a biquaternion algebra to descend from a quadratic extension of the base field, and for a quaternion algebra to descent from a biquadratic extension that is not purely inseparable. Our results extend known results both in characteristic 2 and in characteristic different from 2, see the introduction. Using residue maps for quadratic forms, we show that these invariants do not vanish in general, and we give an explicit central simple algebra of degree 8 and exponent 2 with nonzero invariant, which is therefore indecomposable. As explained in the appendix, the purely inseparable case is quite different; in particular, a quaternion algebra descents if and only if its Brauer class also does.

papers.title: The generalized core-EP inverse of operator matrices with generalized Schur complements
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the generalized core-EP inverse of block operator matrices over a Banach algebra. As a result, novel representations and explicit formulae for the core and core-EP inverses of the $2\times 2$ block operator matrices are established.

papers.title: Moore-Postnikov supcation of simplicial sets and applications in simplicial algebras
papers.abstract: We revisit a canonical filtration of simplicial algebras coming from the Moore-Postnikov system and provide several applications in studying the structure and classification of simplicial algebras and simplicial modules.

papers.title: Extended $\mathcal{O}$-operators on Lie-Yamaguti Algebras
papers.abstract: We study balanced extended $\mathcal O$-operators on Lie--Yamaguti algebras. The construction links operator equations, algebra splittings and Yang--Baxter equations. We build a double from a representation and a balanced equivariant map. The graphs of extended $\mathcal O$-operators are exactly its subalgebras complementary to the first summand. We define extended post-Lie--Yamaguti algebras and prove their two-way relation with extended $\mathcal O$-operators. The tensor form gives a balanced extended Lie--Yamaguti Yang--Baxter equation. We construct a curved $L_\infty[1]$-algebra whose Maurer--Cartan elements are extended $\mathcal O$-operators. The normal representation of a graph gives a cohomology theory for infinitesimal deformations, rigidity and obstructions. We include both cyclic conditions in the lowest paired degree. We also map operator infinitesimals to the deformation cohomology of the induced algebra. Examples give obstructed infinitesimals, rigid scalar operators and nontrivial formal deformations.

papers.title: Kupershmidt--Nijenhuis structures on pre-Leibniz algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first construct the dual of a representation of a pre-Leibniz algebra and study infinitesimal deformations of a pre-Leibniz algebra with a representation, which lead to Nijenhuis pairs, characterizing trivial deformations, and to dual-Nijenhuis pairs. Building on these notions, we introduce Kupershmidt-(dual-)Nijenhuis structures and show that they give rise to hierarchies of pairwise compatible Kupershmidt operators, the converse holding under an invertibility condition. Finally, we show that Rota--Baxter--Nijenhuis structures, $r$-$n$ structures and BN-structures all arise as particular cases, and that the first two correspond to each other on quadratic pre-Leibniz algebras.

papers.title: Anti-quadratic nearly associative algebras
papers.abstract: An anti-quadratic nearly associative algebra $(A, \bullet, \omega)$ is a nearly associative algebra equipped with a non-degenerate skew-symmetric bilinear form $\omega$ satisfying the anti-associativity condition $\omega(u \bullet v, w) = -\omega(u, v \bullet w)$ for all $u, v, w \in A.$ In this paper, we investigate the structural properties and extension theory of these algebras. We prove that any anti-quadratic nearly associative algebra is inherently nilpotent of index at most $6$. Furthermore, we introduce a novel $T T^*$-extension method and show that every anti-quadratic nearly associative algebra arises from this construction. We also introduce the notion of a double extension and prove that every such algebra can be constructed by iterated double extensions. Finally, as an application, we give a complete classification of anti-quadratic nearly associative algebras of dimension at most $4$.

papers.title: Quasi-projective dimensions over homological ring epimorphisms
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study quasi-projective dimensions of modules over rings connected by homological ring epimorphisms. We establish several inequalities relating the quasi-projective dimensions over the source and target rings. As applications, we investigate the quasi-global dimension of triangular matrix rings and provide examples showing that the class of modules with finite quasi-projective dimension does not satisfy the 2-out-of-3 property in general.

papers.title: P-generalized determinant over quaternions and its applications
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the ${\rm P}$-generalized determinant, a more general class of quaternion determinants. It unifies several classical quaternion determinants proposed between 1922 and 2008, including the Moore determinant, the Xie determinant, the Chen determinant, and the Kyrchei row--column determinants, thereby revealing the essential nature of quaternion determinants as multivariate polynomial-type functions with a fixed ordering of products. We provide equivalent characterizations of the expansion of the $\mathrm{P}$-generalized determinant along a given row or column, and establish conversion relations between the $\mathrm{P}_{l}$- and $\mathrm{P}_{r}$-generalized determinants. We prove that the $\mathrm{P}$-generalized determinant of a quaternion Hermitian matrix is a real number independent of the choice of cycle representation rule. We further investigate the behavior of the $\mathrm{P}$-generalized determinant under elementary row and column operations on quaternion Hermitian matrices, as well as its linearity in rows and columns. Finally, using the $\mathrm{P}$-generalized determinant, we derive determinantal representations of the inverse of an invertible quaternion Hermitian matrix and of the unique solution to the quaternion matrix equation $AXB=C$. In particular, this yields Cramer's rule for the left and right linear systems $Ax=b$ and $xA=b$.

papers.title: Derived tame monomial algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that a finite-dimensional connected monomial algebra over an algebraically closed field is derived tame if and only if every finite connected convex subcategory of its universal cover has non-negative Euler form. Derived tameness is also equivalent to tameness of its repetitive category and trivial extension. For one-cycle algebras, this condition is equivalent to the non-negativity on $\mathbb R$ of $|Q_0|$ explicitly computable polynomials in $\mathbb Q[t]$. This gives a finite algorithm for deciding derived tameness. We also construct an infinite family of derived-tame one-cycle string algebras with minimal cubic relations, no two of which are derived equivalent.

papers.title: Coring morphisms presenting nonaffine noncommutative fibre bundles
papers.abstract: We consider noncommutative analogues of associated fibre bundles where the total space, base space and even the fiber may be nonaffine, that is, not represented by a single algebra, and where the structure group is replaced by a Hopf algebra $H$. We choose to describe gluing of affine pieces by corings. In the role of a principal bundle we take an internal $E$-coring $M$ in the monoidal category of right $H$-comodules where $E$ is a faithfully flat right Hopf-Galois extension. In a role of a fibre we either take a left $H$-comodule algebra $F$, or more generally an internal $F$-coring $N$ in the monoidal category of left $H$-comodules. Cotensor products combining these data is used to obtain an ordinary coring representing the total space of an associated bundle. If the fiber coring $N$ is equipped with a choice of an $H$-coinvariant grouplike element, then we exhibit a canonical morphisms of corings from the $H$-coinvariant coring of $M$ to the associated bundle coring which is viewed as a dual to the projection of an associated bundle.

papers.title: Spectra of stochastic matrices with a Toeplitz interior
papers.abstract: For stochastic matrices of order $n$, the Karpelevi\v{c} region is the set of all possible eigenvalues. We study matrices whose first and last $m$ rows are arbitrary probability vectors, while the remaining middle rows come from one probability vector by successive cyclic shifts to the right, moving the last entry to the first position each time. As $m$ increases, their eigenvalue regions expand from the polygon spanned by the $n$th roots of unity. For $n\ge3$, they first equal the full Karpelevi\v{c} region at $m=\lceil(n-1)/4\rceil$. Reproducing all $n$ eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity, of every stochastic matrix of the same order requires $m=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. Thus, in even order $n\ge4$, retaining two consecutive rows with the Toeplitz pattern can exclude eigenvalue lists even when every possible eigenvalue occurs individually. The boundary of the Karpelevi\v{c} region consists of arcs joining roots of unity. We determine the least $m$ for which every point of each arc occurs as an eigenvalue in our family. For arcs whose nonreal points first become possible eigenvalues at order $n\ge4$, and for $m\ge1$ below this minimum, no point on the arc other than its endpoints occurs in the family. At the minimum, every point on the arc becomes attainable. At the smallest order $n\ge4$ at which a nonreal point on a boundary arc away from its endpoints can occur as an eigenvalue, that point determines the characteristic polynomial of every stochastic matrix of order $n$ having it as an eigenvalue. Further results describe the smaller regions and the angles at which their boundaries approach roots of unity.

papers.title: The Fundamental theorem of tropical differential algebra over nontrivially valued fields and the radius of convergence of nonarchimedean differential equations
papers.abstract: We prove a fundamental theorem for tropical partial differential equations, analogous to the fundamental theorem of tropical geometry in this context. We extend results from Aroca et al., Falkensteiner et al. and from Fink and Toghani for the case of trivial valuation as introduced by Grigoriev to differential equations with power series coefficients over any valued field. Crucial ingredients are the framework for tropical partial differential equations introduced by Giansiracusa and Mereta and a result on infinite intersections of projections of fibers of tropicalizations, which we prove using Hrushovski and Loeser's model-theoretic interpretation of Berkovich analytification. As a corollary of the fundamental theorem, we show that the radius of convergence of solutions of an ordinary differential equation over a nontrivially valued field can be computed tropically.

papers.title: A stacky resolution of singularities for orders by Azumaya algebras
papers.abstract: We construct a stacky resolution of singularities for certain noncommutative spaces which can be viewed as 'finite noncommutative extensions' of schemes. More precisely, we show that any order over a reduced separated finite type scheme over a field of characteristic zero can be resolved by an Azumaya algebra over a smooth Deligne--Mumford stack by a sequence of stacky blow-ups.

papers.title: Pure dimension and counterexamples to the maximality of purely-primes
papers.abstract: In analogy with the notion of Krull dimension, for every commutative ring $R$, we introduce the notion of pure dimension $\pdim(R)$ by considering chains of purely-prime ideals. Then we see that the inequality $\pdim(R)\leqslant\dim(R)$ holds for a very broad class of rings $R$, including pseudo-Noetherian rings (e.g., Noetherian rings), Gelfand rings (e.g., local rings), mp-rings (e.g., integral domains), and rings with finitely many maximal ideals or finitely many minimal primes. In fact, for all of these rings $R$, we always have $\pdim(R)=0$, i.e., every purely-prime ideal of $R$ is purely-maximal. \\ However, we prove a classification theorem which states for each ordinal number $\Omega$ the proper pure ideals of the commutative ring $$R_{\Omega}=k[X_{\alpha} : \alpha <\Omega]/\big(X_{\alpha}(1-X_{\beta}) : \alpha<\beta<\Omega\big)$$ are exactly of the form $I_{\lambda}=(x_{\alpha}: \alpha<\lambda)$ with $\lambda=0$ or $\lambda\leqslant\Omega$ a limit ordinal (we write $x_{\alpha}$ for the image of $X_{\alpha}$ in $R_{\Omega}$). In addition, all of them are purely-prime ideals and form the following unique strictly ascending chain: $$I_{0}=0\subset I_{\omega}\subset I_{\omega\cdot2}\subset I_{\omega\cdot 3}\subset\ldots\subset I_{\omega\cdot\alpha}$$ where $\alpha$ is a unique ordinal with $\Omega=\omega\cdot\alpha+n$ and $n\in\omega$. To prove this theorem, we use the full strength of ...

papers.title: Coherent configurations and Frobenius structures
papers.abstract: We prove that coherent configurations can be represented as modules over Frobenius structures in the category of real nonnegative matrices. We generalize the notion of admissible morphism from association schemes to coherent configurations. We show that the Frobenius structure associated to a coherent configuration can be modified to become a dagger Frobenius structure, and use this to connect the coherent configurations to groupoids and $H^*$-algebras. We examine the properties of the dagger Frobenius structure with respect to admissible morphisms. We introduce the matrix $O$ obtained as the composition of comultiplication and multiplication of the dagger Frobenius structure and prove that we may obtain the valencies of colors, and thus recover the original coherent configuration, as an eigenvector of $O$. In the last part of the paper, we examine the spectrum of $O$ and apply it to generalize the Lagrange theorem from groups to association schemes.

papers.title: On classifications of third- and fourth-order symmetric tensors by eigenvalues
papers.abstract: This paper addresses two fundamental problems posed by Qi regarding the sufficiency of eigenvalues for the classification of symmetric tensors in the two-dimensional setting. For $2\times2\times2$ and $2\times2\times2\times2$ complex symmetric tensors, we classify their equivalence classes using canonical forms of their associated binary cubics and quartics. We then determine the number of eigenpair classes and the multiplicities of zero eigenvalues for the canonical forms over the complex domain. We demonstrate that these spectral counts do not distinguish all real equivalence classes. Finally, we extend this approach to derive canonical forms and classification for real third- and fourth-order linear partial differential equations in two variables using their bijective relationship to binary forms.

papers.title: Pseudo-Euclidean Novikov Superalgebras: Structure and Properties
papers.abstract: A pseudo-Euclidean Novikov superalgebra $A$ is a Novikov superalgebra endowed with a non-degenerate symmetric bilinear form $\langle, \rangle$ such that all left multiplication operators are $\langle, \rangle$-antisymmetric. In this case, the associated Lie superalgebra $(A^{-},\langle, \rangle)$ is a flat pseudo-Euclidean Lie superalgebra. In this paper, we investigate the structure of pseudo-Euclidean Novikov superalgebras. In particular, we introduce a distinguished subclass, called \emph{Milnor superalgebras}, and prove that any pseudo-Euclidean Novikov superalgebra whose two-sided ideal is non-degenerate belongs to this class. We provide a method for constructing pseudo-Euclidean Novikov superalgebras. We also introduce a double extension procedure for pseudo-Euclidean Novikov superalgebras and show that every such superalgebra with a degenerate two-sided ideal can be obtained via this method. Furthermore, we establish that any pseudo-Euclidean Novikov superalgebra is either a Milnor superalgebra or can be obtained by a sequence of double extensions starting from a Milnor superalgebra. As an application, we provide a complete classification of pseudo-Euclidean Novikov superalgebras of total dimension at most four over the field of real numbers.

papers.title: Brauer graph algebras are closed under stable equivalence of Morita type
papers.abstract: We study stable equivalences of Brauer graph algebras. We prove that a basic symmetric algebra without semisimple summands which is stably equivalent to a Brauer graph algebra is again a Brauer graph algebra. In particular, Brauer graph algebras are closed up to semisimple summands under stable equivalence of Morita type. As consequences, we reprove the closure under derived equivalence established by Antipov and Zvonareva and obtain a solution of the reconstruction problem posed by Rickard and Rouquier for algebras stably equivalent of Morita type to Brauer graph algebras.
